Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test case `testToClass_object()` calls `ClassUtils.toClass` with an Object array containing `{"Test", null, 99d}` and expects an array of classes `{String.class, null, Double.class}`. The current bug report states that `m0(Object[])` (which we confirm to be `ClassUtils.toClass(Object[])`) throws a NullPointerException (NPE) on null array elements. Examining the source code of `ClassUtils.toClass`, we see the method does:

- If the input array is null, returns null.
- If empty, returns an empty Class array.
- Otherwise, initializes a Class<?> array of the same length.
- Iterates through all elements, and directly calls `array[i].getClass()` to set the class at the same index.

The critical issue is that the code does not check if the element at index i is null before calling `getClass()`. Since the test passes an explicit null in the array, the method will throw a NullPointerException at that index. 

The test expects that null elements map to null entries in the resulting Class array, but the method does not handle this case at all. This directly explains the test failure and matches the summary describing the NPE on null array element.

Recent bug reports are about ArrayUtils adding issues and type problems, which are unrelated. The core problem is a missing null check in `ClassUtils.toClass` on input array elements when determining their class.

The fix would be to change this method to check if `array[i]` is null and assign null to `classes[i]` in that case instead of calling `getClass()` unconditionally.

This root cause and suggested fix fully explain the observed failure.

---

Next, I will identify which method(s) are the appropriate locations for this fix.
ClassUtils.toClass(java.lang.Object[])

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
